title: Windows 11 November preview: web sign-in on hybrid join
summary: KB5132057, the optional non-security preview for Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2 (builds 26200.10075 and 26300.10075), shipped on 19 November 2026 and brings web sign-in to Microsoft Entra hybrid joined devices, not only Entra joined ones. Users can sign in at the lock screen with a FIDO2 key, a phone passkey or a Temporary Access Pass, and Windows still gets a Kerberos ticket for on-prem shares and sites; the same gradual rollout adds the face sign-in brightening option, an NFC tap indicator for security keys and the new Windows Search. Fixes include the misleading 'Something went wrong' error on Android during cross-device passkey sign-in and KMS/token-based activation failures on Windows IoT Enterprise LTSC. Microsoft says there will be no December non-security preview; the December security update is not affected.
why: Web sign-in on hybrid joined devices removes the main blocker for TAP-based onboarding and passwordless shared PCs in estates that still run hybrid join. It is a gradual-rollout feature, so a pilot device may not show it straight away. The known issue that matters for server teams is SQL Server linked-server queries over OLE DB leaving connections open; Microsoft lists an out-of-band fix 'in the next few days' and a support-only mitigation.
todo: Do now: put KB5132057 on a pilot ring of hybrid joined devices and test web sign-in with TAP and a FIDO2 key, including access to an on-prem file share after sign-in (Kerberos).
Check that your web sign-in policy (Authentication/EnableWebSignIn) is scoped to the pilot only before you widen it.

Wait: the feature arrives by gradual rollout; do not treat a missing tile on one device as a failure. Watch release health for the OLE DB out-of-band update before rolling the December cumulative to SQL hosts.
effective_note: Optional preview update; features in gradual rollout — per Microsoft.
